title: The Birds, the Beasts, and the Bat
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: The Birds were at war with the Beasts, and many battles were fought with varying success on either side. The Bat did not throw in his lot definitely with either party, but when things went well for the Birds he was found fighting in their ranks; when, on the other hand, the Beasts got the upper hand, he was to be found among the Beasts.

No one paid any attention to him while the war lasted: but when it was over, and peace was restored, neither the Birds nor the Beasts would have anything to do with so double-faced a traitor, and so he remains to this day a solitary outcast from both.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is at war at the start of the story?
options: The Bats and the Birds
The Beasts and the Insects
The Birds and the Beasts
The Birds and the Fish

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whose side does the Bat fight on when the Birds are winning?
options: The Birds
The Beasts
Neither side at all
Whichever side is losing

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whose side does the Bat fight on when the Beasts are winning?
options: The Birds
He refuses to fight at all
He fights for both sides equally
The Beasts

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much attention does anyone pay the Bat while the war lasts?
options: Everyone watches him closely
No one pays any attention to him
Only the Birds notice his behavior
Only the Beasts notice his behavior

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happens once peace is restored?
options: Both sides welcome the Bat as a hero
The Birds punish the Bat, but the Beasts forgive him
Neither side will have anything to do with the Bat
The Beasts punish the Bat, but the Birds forgive him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Bat become after the war ends?
options: A solitary outcast from both
A respected leader among the Birds
A trusted advisor to the Beasts
A wanderer who starts a new group

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Bat keep switching sides during the war?
options: He is confused about which side he truly belongs to
He is trying to end the war by joining both equally
He is ordered to switch by a higher authority
He wants to always be seen as part of the winning side

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Bat's strategy fail once the war is over?
options: The war never actually ends, so he never gets the chance to rest
Both sides now see through his shifting loyalty and reject him for it
He forgets which side he supported most often
He is punished specifically by the side that lost

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "double-faced" mean in "so double-faced a traitor"?
options: Having two literal faces
Extremely brave in battle
Deceitful, showing two different loyalties
Unable to make any decision at all

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Constantly switching loyalty to whoever is winning leaves you trusted by no one in the end
Wars always end with one clear winner and one clear loser
Bats are naturally suited to being both birds and beasts
Neutral parties are always safest during any conflict

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the passage describe the fighting between the Birds and Beasts?
options: One side won every single battle
The war ended after only one battle
Neither side ever gained an advantage
Many battles were fought with varying success on either side

questions.prompt: According to the passage, did the Bat commit definitely to either side at the start?
options: Yes, he joined the Birds from the very beginning
No, he did not throw in his lot definitely with either party
Yes, he joined the Beasts from the very beginning
No, he refused to take part in the war at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when is peace finally restored?
options: Immediately after the first battle
Only after the Bat intervened
After the war has been going on for some time
Only after the Birds fully surrendered

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does no one notice the Bat's behavior while the war is happening?
options: Everyone is too focused on the battles themselves to track individual loyalty
The Bat hides himself well during every battle
The Bat only switches sides once the war has ended
Both sides secretly approve of his behavior during the war

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Bat's fate suggest about trying to please everyone by taking no firm stand?
options: It is generally the safest strategy during any conflict
It works well as long as the conflict never ends
It earns respect from both sides in the long run
It can ultimately leave you belonging to no group at all

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "outcast" mean in "a solitary outcast from both"?
options: Someone chosen as a leader
Someone rejected and excluded by a group
Someone respected by all sides
Someone who wins every argument

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Bat ends the war between the Birds and Beasts
A Bat joins the Birds permanently after the war
A Bat switches sides throughout a war to stay with the winners, and afterward is rejected by both sides
A Bat is punished only by the Beasts after the war
